One kind, `base_type`, which a `value_type` names as its `base` and which no data element, argument, record field or array element names. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.
layers.label: Base Types

kinds.description: A base type: how the platform stores a value — its size in bits, its encoding and its C declaration — emitted as a `SW-BASE-TYPE`. A base type is never what a data prototype is typed by (AUTOSAR's `AutosarDataPrototype.type`): no data element, argument, record field or array element may name one. A base type is an element of its own layer, `base_types`, so it may share its name with a type of another layer. A `value_type` names it as its `base`, and the data prototypes name the `value_type`.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/base/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the base types, must not be blank, and immutable.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Always `base_type`. The layer holds one kind and is not discriminated; the field is an ordinary literal, kept, immutable as it was, so a base type file reads as it did when base types were a kind of the data types layer.

fields.name: size
fields.description: The size of the base type, in bits. Must be > 0.

fields.name: encoding
fields.description: A required AUTOSAR BASE-TYPE-ENCODING token (NONE, 2C, IEEE754, ...); must not be blank, because a blank one is not round-trippable through the ARXML importer.

fields.name: native_declaration
fields.description: The C type name the generated code declares for this base type (for example `uint8_t`), emitted exactly as written as its `NATIVE-DECLARATION`. Required by check-model: SWCraft never derives one, so a base type without it still loads, but check-model reports it and ARXML generation refuses it until it is filled in.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: package
fields.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Base`, its layer's package, this base type is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the base type and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Base/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Base` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/DataTypes/Base/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/DataTypes/Base` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

layers.name: requirements
layers.description: Requirements and specification items, identified by `id` rather than `name`; the architecture elements that realize one name it in their own `satisfies`. An architecture requirement is published in the generated `needs.json` as a need of its own; an imported one is never published, only named by its id in the links that reach it.
layers.label: Requirements

kinds.description: One requirement or specification item. Identified by `id` rather than `name`, and its file is named from the `id`; the elements that realize it name it in their `satisfies` as `<id>@<version>`, so the requirement file names no element and an imported one can be overwritten by a re-import without losing a link, or removed by one when the delivery no longer holds it. `document`, `baseline` and `revision` record where an external requirement came from. An architecture requirement is published in the generated `needs.json` as a need of its own; an imported one is never published, only named by its id in the links that reach it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The requirement's identity; the file is named from it (`requirements/{id}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the layer, must not be empty, and immutable. It is the need's id in the generated `needs.json`, as written, and the id a link to the requirement names there. It may not contain `@` or `:`, the separators of a link's version and of an element reference.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The requirement's one-line title; an architecture requirement's published need carries it as its title.

fields.name: description
fields.description: The requirement's statement; an architecture requirement's published need carries it as its content. Required: a requirement without a statement is not one.

fields.name: req_type
fields.description: `req` for a requirement, `spec` for a specification item; an architecture requirement is published as the need type `arch_req` or `arch_spec`.

fields.name: version
fields.description: SWCraft's own change counter for this requirement, a positive integer: 1 when the requirement is first written, unless a link the requirements import leaves in the model as it was already names its id at a version, when the import writes it above every such version, so no link made before reads as confirmed against its text. The requirements import raises it by one when an external requirement's text, level, type or parents change; for an architecture requirement the author raises it, and no SWCraft edit raises it. A link `REQ-12@3` is confirmed for version 3; a link naming another version is reported as needing confirmation, and a bare `REQ-12` as a version not stated. It is never the source tool's revision, which is `revision`.

fields.name: source
fields.description: Who owns the file: `external`, a requirement an importer writes from a requirements tool, which a re-import overwrites, and removes when the delivery no longer holds it; or `architecture`, a requirement authored in the architecture model. No default: provenance is stated, never assumed. Nothing refuses an edit of an external requirement; the importer's workflow is what keeps it read-only.

fields.name: derived_from
fields.description: What this requirement is derived from: a requirement, as `<id>@<version>` exactly as in `satisfies`, or a top-level architecture element, as `<token>:<name>` with the token of the `swc`, `interfaces`, `compositions`, `tasks` or `hardware` layer (`hardware:Core0`, `swc:SpeedCtrlSWC`). A member is an element reference when its text before the first `:` is one of those five tokens; a requirement `id` never contains `:`. Only the requirement form is a member of the relation; an element reference is resolved by `check-model` alone. Omitted while empty.

relation.summary: Each requirement-form member of a requirement's derived_from names a parent requirement by its `id`, the version after the first `@` taking no part in the resolution; an element-form member is not a member of the relation. A relation and not a reference, because the members are whole-value collection entries rather than a field whose value is one identity.

fields.name: asil
fields.description: The safety integrity level allocated to this requirement: `QM`, `A`, `B`, `C` or `D`, or a decomposed `X(Y)` such as `B(D)` — the thirteen spellings the AUTOSAR Safety Extensions list — where `Y` is the level before decomposition. Every rule ranks by `X`; one rule, `trace.decomposition-context-mismatch`, compares a requirement's `(Y)` with the level its parent requirement had before decomposition. Absent when none is allocated. A written `QM`, `QM(Y)` included, declares that none is — ISO 26262-1 calls QM not an ASIL, so it is not the lowest level — and is read as a declaration rather than as an absence. A component that declares no level of its own takes the highest level of the requirements its own `satisfies`, its ports' and its runnables' name.

fields.name: document
fields.description: The source document this requirement was taken from, as the requirements tool names it (a document name, number or module). Provenance only: no check reads it, and a change of it never moves `version`. Absent when unknown.

fields.name: baseline
fields.description: The version of the requirements delivery this requirement was last imported from — the requirements team's baseline or commit, given to the import or taken from the file's version. Provenance only: no check reads it, and a change of it never moves `version`. Absent on an architecture requirement and on a stub.

fields.name: revision
fields.description: The source tool's own revision of this requirement, exactly as the tool writes it (`7`, `1.3`, `B`). It is the revision a reader outside SWCraft sees; `version` is SWCraft's own change counter and is never shown in its place. Provenance only: no check reads it, and a change of it never moves `version`. Absent when unknown.

fields.name: stub
fields.description: True for a placeholder the import created for a parent requirement that `derived_from` names but that neither the import file nor the model holds. Every other field is still required: its title and description are placeholders the import writes, not the parent's requirement text, and it is replaced when an import brings the parent, and removed when nothing in the model names it any longer; every stub is reported as a warning. Only a YAML boolean loads, and YAML itself reads an unquoted `yes`, `on`, `no` or `off` as one; a quoted `'true'` or a `1` is refused. Absent on every real requirement.

layers.name: compositions
layers.description: Composition types, one file each: the structural hierarchy of the architecture. A composition declares boundary ports of its own, holds named members that instantiate declared component and composition types, and delegates its ports to its members'. The hierarchy is by reference exactly as AUTOSAR spells it — a member names a type rather than nesting it — so the directory stays flat however deep the instantiation goes.
layers.label: Compositions

kinds.description: One composition type: an AUTOSAR `COMPOSITION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE`. It declares the boundary ports it offers and requires, the members it contains — each a named instance of a declared component or composition type — and the delegations that wire a boundary port through to a member's port. Assembly connectors are not held here: a connector names the composition it belongs to from its own file.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The composition's identity; the file is named from it (`compositions/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the layer, must not be empty, and immutable — renaming is a remove and a create. It is emitted as the `COMPOSITION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE`'s `SHORT-NAME`, so it must be a legal AUTOSAR Identifier.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The human-readable title shown on the composition's frame in the diagrams and, when it differs from `name`, written into the generated ARXML as the composition's `LONG-NAME`, exactly as held. A title equal to the name writes none: the `SHORT-NAME` already carries it.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the composition, shown when the pointer rests on its frame in the diagrams, when non-empty, and written into the generated ARXML as the composition type's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: root
fields.description: Whether this composition is the top of the hierarchy. Exactly one composition in a project declares `true`: it is the one the ARXML writer emits at the top, and the one an assembly connector belongs to when it names none. Left out of the file while it is `false`, so only the root carries the key.

fields.name: ports
fields.description: The composition's boundary ports, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the composition. Each is typed by a declared interface and is reached from outside like any component's port; a delegation is what carries it through to a member.

fields.name: members
fields.description: The components and compositions this one contains, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the composition. One member is one AUTOSAR `SW-COMPONENT-PROTOTYPE`: a name of its own and the type it instantiates. A type may stand in several compositions, but never twice in one — a connector endpoint names the type, and it must resolve to a single member.

fields.name: delegations
fields.description: The wiring from this composition's own boundary ports to its members' ports, addressed by `name`, which must be unique inside the composition. Each becomes one AUTOSAR `DELEGATION-SW-CONNECTOR`.

fields.name: package
fields.description: The one sub-package of `/ComponentTypes` this composition is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the composition and every reference to it take `/ComponentTypes/{package}/`. Absent means `/ComponentTypes` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/ComponentTypes/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/ComponentTypes` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

fields.name: satisfies
fields.description: The requirements this composition satisfies, each as the requirement's `id` and, after `@`, the version the link was confirmed for (`REQ-12@3`); a bare `id` is reported as a version not stated, and a version other than the requirement's as a link needing confirmation. A link is added or removed, never edited in place. It allocates no ASIL to anything.

relation.summary: Each member of a composition's satisfies names a requirement by its `id`, the version after the first `@` taking no part in the resolution. A relation and not a reference, because the members are whole-value collection entries rather than a field whose value is one identity.

kinds.description: One boundary port of a composition: a named, directed endpoint typed by an interface. A `provide` port offers the interface to whatever contains the composition, a `require` port consumes it, and a delegation carries either through to a member's port of the same direction. It declares the same four fields as `kind:swc.port` and the duplication is deliberate: a bare kind name is unique across the whole contract and `memberOf` is derived per layer, so one kind cannot be a member of two layers' elements.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The port's identity inside its composition; unique among the composition's ports and immutable.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: Whether the port offers the interface (`provide`) or consumes it (`require`). A delegation joins a boundary port to a member's port of the same direction — it carries the port outward rather than connecting two ends.

fields.name: interface
fields.description: The name of the declared interface this port is typed by. The member port it delegates to need not name the same interface, as long as the two are compatible.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the boundary port. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

kinds.description: One member of a composition: an AUTOSAR `SW-COMPONENT-PROTOTYPE`. It carries a name of its own — the address the composition's delegations use — and exactly one of `type`, naming a declared software component, or `composition`, naming another declared composition. The two fields are the model's spelling of the `TYPE-TREF`'s `DEST`, and each resolves into its own layer; a member declaring neither, or both, is refused.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The member's identity inside its composition; unique among the composition's members and immutable. It is written even when it equals the type it instantiates, and it is emitted as the `SW-COMPONENT-PROTOTYPE`'s `SHORT-NAME`, so it must be a legal AUTOSAR Identifier.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The name of the declared software component this member instantiates. Exactly one of `type` and `composition` is set, and this one is emitted with `DEST` `APPLICATION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE`. A component may be placed in several compositions but never twice in one.

fields.name: composition
fields.description: The name of the declared composition this member instantiates. Exactly one of `type` and `composition` is set, and this one is emitted with `DEST` `COMPOSITION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE`. It is the edge that makes the hierarchy: a composition that transitively contains itself is refused.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the member. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

kinds.description: One delegation of a composition: an AUTOSAR `DELEGATION-SW-CONNECTOR`. It joins one of the composition's own boundary ports to a port of one of its members, so that what the composition offers or requires at its boundary is served by a component inside it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The delegation's identity inside its composition; unique among the composition's delegations and immutable. It is emitted as the `DELEGATION-SW-CONNECTOR`'s `SHORT-NAME`, so it must be a legal AUTOSAR Identifier.

fields.name: port
fields.description: The name of one of this composition's own boundary ports — the outer end of the delegation.

fields.name: member
fields.description: The name of one of this composition's members — the instance the delegation reaches into. A member name and never a type name: a delegation addresses the instance, which is what makes one type placeable more than once.

fields.name: member_port
fields.description: The name of a port of that member's type — the inner end of the delegation. Its direction must match the outer port's.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the delegation. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

layers.name: tasks
layers.description: OS tasks and the runnables each one executes. `period` is in seconds; a budget, `wcet`, carries its own unit.
layers.label: Tasks

kinds.description: One OS task: a periodic schedulable unit with a priority, a partition assignment, an optional worst-case execution budget and the ordered list of runnables it executes. A task's period must be a divisor of every timing period among the runnables it maps.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The task's identity; the file is named from it (`tasks/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the layer, must not be empty, and immutable.

fields.name: period
fields.description: The task's activation period, in seconds (a budget, `wcet`, carries its own unit). Must be > 0.

fields.name: priority
fields.description: Must be >= 0; higher is more urgent.

fields.name: partition
fields.description: The name of the partition this task runs in; the task runs on that partition's core. It must name a `partition` declared under `hardware/`.

fields.name: wcet
fields.description: The task's execution-time budget: what the architect allots to the task, an upper bound the model is checked against and never a measurement. Written as a whole number followed by its unit, one of `ns`, `us`, `ms` or `s` — `1200us`, `2ms` — with no space, no leading zero, no decimal point and at most 18 digits; omitted or `null` when no budget is declared, greater than zero when present, and a `strict` core budget requires one on every task of that core. Analysis input only: the standard's execution-time constraint names an executable entity, and an OS task is none, so no ARXML output carries it. A file still spelling `wcet_us` is refused with the new spelling.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the task. Carried in the model; it reaches no generated artifact.

fields.name: runnables
fields.description: The runnables the task executes, in order, each naming its component by exactly one of `swc` and `instance`, and its `runnable`; an entry written the same way appears at most once in a task.

fields.name: coexistence
fields.description: The argument for scheduling components of different safety integrity levels together in this task, as free text. Declaring one stops the task being reported for mixing levels. It answers mixing by execution time inside this task; the partition's own `coexistence` answers mixing by memory. It is a declaration and not a verification: the text is checked against nothing, and the model expresses no memory protection and no schedule isolation — so a task carrying an argument is argued, never shown to be free of interference. Legal on a task whose components are rated alike, where nothing reads it yet.

fields.name: satisfies
fields.description: The requirements this task satisfies, each as the requirement's `id` and, after `@`, the version the link was confirmed for (`REQ-12@3`); a bare `id` is reported as a version not stated, and a version other than the requirement's as a link needing confirmation. A link is added or removed, never edited in place. It allocates no ASIL to anything.

relation.summary: Each member of a task's satisfies names a requirement by its `id`, the version after the first `@` taking no part in the resolution. A relation and not a reference, because the members are whole-value collection entries rather than a field whose value is one identity.

kinds.description: One entry of a task's `runnables` list: a runnable of a software component, the component named by exactly one of `swc` (a component type placed at most once below the root composition, or not at all) and `instance` (one occurrence of a component below the root composition). The `(swc, instance, runnable)` triple, the absent selector as `null`, is the member's identity, because runnable names are unique only inside their own component.

fields.name: swc
fields.description: The name of the declared software component that owns the runnable; exactly one of `swc` and `instance` is set. Part of the member's composite identity, and so immutable.

fields.name: instance
fields.description: The occurrence of a component below the root composition whose runnable this is, as a `/`-joined path of composition member names from the root composition down — a member of the root is its member name alone, a nested one `outer/inner` — never starting with the root composition's own name; exactly one of `swc` and `instance` is set. Part of the member's composite identity, and so immutable.

fields.name: runnable
fields.description: The name of a runnable of that component. Part of the composite identity, and so immutable; a runnable of one resolved component is mapped to at most one task across the model.

layers.name: sequences
layers.description: Sequence scenarios, one task each; each is drawn as a sequence diagram whose files are named from the scenario's name.
layers.label: Sequences

kinds.description: One sequence scenario: an ordered walk through some of the runnables of exactly one task, drawn as a sequence diagram. The steps must follow the task's own runnable order.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The scenario's identity, which also names its sequence diagram's files. Must match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ — a rule of this layer alone, deliberately not the AUTOSAR `Identifier` rule.

fields.name: task
fields.description: The name of the declared task this scenario walks; exactly one per scenario, and every step must be mapped to it.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The scenario's human-readable title, shown after its name in the heading of its sequence diagram (`sd {name} — {title}`). When empty, the heading is the name alone.

fields.name: steps
fields.description: The steps of the scenario, in order. Must not be empty and must be an ordered subsequence of the referenced task's runnables.

kinds.description: One step of a sequence scenario: the runnable it shows, its component named by exactly one of `swc` and `instance`, with an optional note. The `(swc, instance, runnable)` triple, the absent selector as `null`, is the step's identity; the step must be mapped to the scenario's task, and a step written the same way appears at most once per scenario.

fields.name: swc
fields.description: The name of the declared software component the step runs in; exactly one of `swc` and `instance` is set. Part of the step's composite identity, and so immutable.

fields.name: instance
fields.description: The occurrence of a component below the root composition the step runs in, as a `/`-joined path of composition member names from the root composition down — a member of the root is its member name alone, a nested one `outer/inner` — never starting with the root composition's own name; exactly one of `swc` and `instance` is set. Part of the step's composite identity, and so immutable.

fields.name: runnable
fields.description: The name of a runnable of that component, which must be mapped to the scenario's task. Part of the composite identity, and so immutable.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Free text shown beside the step on its sequence diagram; when non-empty the step's activation is labelled `{runnable} — {note}`.

layers.name: hardware
layers.description: The processor the software runs on, its cores, the partitions its tasks run in, and the memories those cores may use. Exactly one processor is declared; every task runs in a declared partition on a declared core, and every memory a component budgets is declared here.
layers.label: Hardware

kinds.description: The one processor the software runs on. Every project declares exactly one. Its cores, its partitions and its memories are elements of this layer in their own right, so a partition, a task or a component names one of them directly rather than through the processor.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The processor's identity; the file is named from it (`hardware/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across every hardware element, and immutable.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: The discriminator that selects this hardware element kind; always `processor`.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the processor — the part it stands for, for instance. Carried in the model; it reaches no generated artifact.

fields.name: satisfies
fields.description: The requirements this processor satisfies, each as the requirement's `id` and, after `@`, the version the link was confirmed for (`REQ-12@3`); a bare `id` is reported as a version not stated, and a version other than the requirement's as a link needing confirmation. A link is added or removed, never edited in place. It allocates no ASIL to anything.

relation.summary: Each member of a processor's satisfies names a requirement by its `id`, the version after the first `@` taking no part in the resolution. A relation and not a reference, because the members are whole-value collection entries rather than a field whose value is one identity.

kinds.description: One schedulable core of the processor, and the CPU-load budget for it. A lockstep pair is one core here, because it executes one instruction stream and the model has nothing to say about the second. Every partition names the core it runs on, and every task runs on its partition's core.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The core's identity; the file is named from it (`hardware/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. It is the name a partition's `core` gives. Unique across every hardware element, and immutable.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: The discriminator that selects this hardware element kind; always `core`.

fields.name: threshold
fields.description: The share of the core's time the tasks mapped to it may total before the budget is breached: a finite fraction in (0, 1]. RAISING it weakens the check, so it is a safety act.

fields.name: enforcement
fields.description: How a breach of this budget is reported. `strict` (the default): every task on the core must declare `wcet` and an over-threshold load is an error. `advisory`: a missing budget counts as zero and a breach is an information line.

fields.name: asil_capability
fields.description: The highest safety integrity level this core, as configured in this project, is declared able to host: `QM`, `A`, `B`, `C` or `D`. The level belongs to the core together with its safety mechanisms, its configuration and the assumptions of use it is qualified under, not to the part alone, and it is the project's own statement: nothing verifies it. Absent when the core is unrated, and then nothing is compared against it; a written `QM` declares that the core hosts no ASIL. A rated partition on this core declaring a higher level is reported, whether or not any task runs in it.

fields.name: hw_id
fields.description: The physical core number the silicon vendor prints in the part's manual, for a reader who has it open. Informational: nothing checks it, and two cores may carry the same one.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the core. Carried in the model; it reaches no generated artifact.

fields.name: satisfies
fields.description: The requirements this core satisfies, each as the requirement's `id` and, after `@`, the version the link was confirmed for (`REQ-12@3`); a bare `id` is reported as a version not stated, and a version other than the requirement's as a link needing confirmation. A link is added or removed, never edited in place. It allocates no ASIL to anything.

relation.summary: Each member of a core's satisfies names a requirement by its `id`, the version after the first `@` taking no part in the resolution. A relation and not a reference, because the members are whole-value collection entries rather than a field whose value is one identity.

kinds.description: One memory of the processor, and the budget for it. It belongs to the processor and names the cores that may use it; every memory a component budgets is one of these.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The memory's identity; the file is named from it (`hardware/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. It is the name a component's `memory` map keys. Unique across every hardware element, and immutable.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: The discriminator that selects this hardware element kind; always `memory`.

fields.name: type
fields.description: What the memory is, in the standard spelling: `RAM`, `ROM`, `EEPROM` or `Flash`. It records the fact for a reader; no check reads it, and all four are budgeted the same way.

fields.name: size
fields.description: The memory's capacity in bytes; must be greater than zero. ENLARGING it weakens the check, so it is a safety act.

fields.name: accessible
fields.description: The cores this project allows to use the memory, by name; at least one, and no repeats. It is a design rule rather than wiring: the integrator configures the processor's memory protection to match it, and no generated artifact does. A list of one core is a memory private to that core. The list is checked against the work placed on each core: a task whose component charges this memory a non-zero budget must run on a core named here. A budget of `0` declares no use and is not checked, which is how a component that runs elsewhere satisfies `strict` enforcement for a memory private to another core. ADMITTING a core weakens that check, so it is a safety act; withdrawing one only makes it refuse more.

relation.summary: Each member of a memory's accessible list names a core by name. A relation and not a reference, because the members are whole-value collection entries rather than a field whose value is one identity.

fields.name: threshold
fields.description: The share of the memory the components' budgets may total before the budget is breached: a finite fraction in (0, 1]. RAISING it weakens the check, so it is a safety act.

fields.name: enforcement
fields.description: How a breach of this budget is reported. `strict` (the default): every component must declare a budget for the memory and an over-threshold total is an error. `advisory`: a missing budget counts as zero and a breach is an information line.

fields.name: asil_capability
fields.description: The highest safety integrity level this memory, as configured in this project, is declared able to host: `QM`, `A`, `B`, `C` or `D`. The level belongs to the memory together with its safety mechanisms, its configuration and the assumptions of use it is qualified under, not to the part alone, and it is the project's own statement: nothing verifies it. Absent when the memory is unrated, and then nothing is compared against it; a written `QM` declares that the memory hosts no ASIL. A component carrying a higher level that charges this memory a non-zero budget is reported; a budget of `0` is not a use.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the memory. Carried in the model; it reaches no generated artifact.

fields.name: satisfies
fields.description: The requirements this memory satisfies, each as the requirement's `id` and, after `@`, the version the link was confirmed for (`REQ-12@3`); a bare `id` is reported as a version not stated, and a version other than the requirement's as a link needing confirmation. A link is added or removed, never edited in place. It allocates no ASIL to anything.

relation.summary: Each member of a memory's satisfies names a requirement by its `id`, the version after the first `@` taking no part in the resolution. A relation and not a reference, because the members are whole-value collection entries rather than a field whose value is one identity.

kinds.description: One partition of the software on a core, AUTOSAR's OS-Application: the tasks that run together on one core under one safety integrity level. Every task names the partition it runs in and takes its core from it. A partition no task names is legal and is checked like any other. On a single core without memory protection AUTOSAR configures no OS-Application at all; the model still has every task name a partition, there one without a level, which is a convention of this model over the standard, as the required `core` is.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The partition's identity; the file is named from it (`hardware/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. It is the name a task's `partition` gives. Unique across every hardware element, and immutable.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: The discriminator that selects this hardware element kind; always `partition`.

fields.name: core
fields.description: The name of the core this partition, and every task in it, runs on. It must name a `core` declared under `hardware/`.

fields.name: asil
fields.description: The safety integrity level the partition is rated at: `QM`, `A`, `B`, `C` or `D`, or a decomposed `X(Y)` such as `B(D)` — the thirteen spellings the AUTOSAR Safety Extensions list — where `Y` is the level before decomposition. Every rule ranks by `X`; one rule, `trace.decomposition-context-mismatch`, compares a requirement's `(Y)` with the level its parent requirement had before decomposition. It is the level the partition is, like a component's `asil`, and not the level it is able to host, like a core's `asil_capability`. Absent when the partition is unrated, and then nothing is compared against it, save that an unrated `trusted` partition is reported beside a partition rated above `QM`; a written `QM`, `QM(Y)` included, rates the partition as hosting no ASIL. A rated partition on a core declared able to host only a lower level is reported, whether or not any task runs in it.

fields.name: trust
fields.description: The class the operating system gives the partition, AUTOSAR's trusted and non-trusted OS-Applications: `non_trusted`, confined by memory protection; `trusted_with_protection`, trusted but confined for memory like a non-trusted one; or `trusted`, unrestricted for memory. Left out of the file while it is `non_trusted`, so a partition file that declares no class is a non-trusted one. It is a declaration and not a verification: nothing in the model expresses the operating system's configuration, so the class is checked only against the levels the partitions declare.

fields.name: coexistence
fields.description: The argument for placing components of different safety integrity levels in this partition, as free text: the memory-mixing argument, where a task's own `coexistence` is the execution-time one. It is a declaration and not a verification: the text is checked against nothing, and the model expresses no memory protection configuration.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the partition. Carried in the model; it reaches no generated artifact.

fields.name: satisfies
fields.description: The requirements this partition satisfies, each as the requirement's `id` and, after `@`, the version the link was confirmed for (`REQ-12@3`); a bare `id` is reported as a version not stated, and a version other than the requirement's as a link needing confirmation. A link is added or removed, never edited in place. It allocates no ASIL to anything.

relation.summary: Each member of a partition's satisfies names a requirement by its `id`, the version after the first `@` taking no part in the resolution. A relation and not a reference, because the members are whole-value collection entries rather than a field whose value is one identity.

layers.name: mapping_sets
layers.description: Data type mapping sets, one file each under `data_types/mapping_sets/`. A set pairs each application type — the physical view of a signal, with its unit, its conversion and its range — with the implementation type that stores it, and a component names the sets its behaviour maps with. Every application type or enumeration a component's ports speak in has to be paired in one of them, because generated code needs to know what stores it. The directory is mandatory and may be empty: a project whose interfaces are typed by implementation types alone needs no set.
layers.label: Mapping Sets

kinds.description: One mapping set, emitted as a `DATA-TYPE-MAPPING-SET`. It holds the pairs that say which implementation type stores each application type. A component references the set as a whole, so one set serves every component that names it, and a project is free to keep one set for the whole model or one per domain.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The set's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/mapping_sets/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the layer, must not be blank, and immutable.

fields.name: maps
fields.description: The pairs the set declares, addressed by the application type each one maps, which appears at most once in a set. The order is the model's and is the order the pairs are emitted in. An empty list is legal and declares nothing.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the set. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: package
fields.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/MappingSets`, its layer's package, this mapping set is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the mapping set and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/MappingSets/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/MappingSets` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/DataTypes/MappingSets/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/DataTypes/MappingSets` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

kinds.description: One pair: the application type, and the implementation type that stores it. Both sides name a declared data type by its own name; which kinds each side may name is checked across files, because the answer is in the type's own file and not here.

fields.name: application
fields.description: The name of the declared application type, enumeration, record or array this pair maps, an element of the `application_types` layer. It is the pair's identity inside the set, and so immutable.

fields.name: implementation
fields.description: The name of the declared value type, reference type, implementation record or implementation array that stores it, and never a pointer. Repointing the pair at another implementation type edits this field; pairing a different application type is a different pair.

layers.name: units
layers.description: Units, one file each under `data_types/units/`: the unit a physical value is measured in, an element a type names by reference. One kind, `unit`, which an application type names as its `unit_ref` and a `linear` compu method as its `unit`. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.
layers.label: Units

kinds.description: A unit, emitted as a `UNIT` in `/DataTypes/Units`: the name a type's physical value is measured in and the text it is shown as. An application type names one by its `unit_ref`, in place of the inline `unit` text, and a `linear` compu method by its `unit`. A unit's SI relation and physical dimension are not held, so every unit has the defaults the standard gives them.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The unit's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/units/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the units, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name.

fields.name: display_name
fields.description: The text the unit is shown as (for example `km/h`), written as the `UNIT`'s `DISPLAY-NAME` exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the unit. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: package
fields.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Units`, its layer's package, this unit is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the unit and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Units/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Units` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

layers.name: compu_methods
layers.description: Computation methods, one file each under `data_types/compu_methods/`: how a stored value becomes the physical or the named one, an element a type names by reference. Two element kinds discriminated by `kind` (`texttable`, `linear`), plus one nested member kind (`table_entry`). An enumeration, a value type and a reference type name a `texttable` by their `compu_method_ref`, an application type names a `linear` by its own. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.
layers.label: Compu Methods

kinds.description: A computation method of category `TEXTTABLE`, emitted as a `COMPU-METHOD` in `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`: a table of named values, one closed single-point `COMPU-SCALE` per entry, the shape an enumeration's own generated method has. An enumeration names one by its `compu_method_ref` in place of inline `literals`, and an implementation value or reference type by its `compu_method_ref`, which is the one way an implementation type states literals.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The compu method's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/compu_methods/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the compu methods, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: The discriminator that selects this compu method kind; always `texttable`.

fields.name: entries
fields.description: The table's named values, addressed by `name`, in the order they are emitted. Must not be empty: a `TEXTTABLE` holds one or more scales.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the compu method. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: package
fields.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`, its layer's package, this compu method is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the compu method and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/CompuMethods/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/CompuMethods` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

kinds.description: A computation method of category `LINEAR`, emitted as a `COMPU-METHOD` in `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`: physical = stored × `factor` + `offset`, one `COMPU-SCALE` in the internal-to-physical direction, referring to the `unit` element it names. An application type names one by its `compu_method_ref`, in place of an inline `conversion`. It holds no scale label, which the standard makes not applicable for a `LINEAR` scale; the scale's limits are its optional `limits`.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The compu method's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/compu_methods/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the compu methods, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: The discriminator that selects this compu method kind; always `linear`.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: The name of the declared unit, an element of the `units` layer, the method refers to: a `LINEAR` computation method refers to a unit. Must not be blank.

fields.name: factor
fields.description: The multiplier applied to the stored value. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: The constant added after the multiplication. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float.

fields.name: limits
fields.description: The limits of the linear computation method's scale, on the stored side: the values the conversion is defined for, which is what the standard reads a scale's limits as -- the limiting values before the conversion is applied. Written as the scale's `LOWER-LIMIT` and `UPPER-LIMIT`. Absent, the scale states no limit and the conversion applies to every stored value; it is not the physical range, which is the type's `range`.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the compu method. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: package
fields.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`, its layer's package, this compu method is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the compu method and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/CompuMethods/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/CompuMethods` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

kinds.description: The limits of a linear computation method's scale, on the stored side. A nested object rather than a list member, so it has no identity of its own and every field of it may change. Either limit may be left out; the lower one must not be above the upper one, and the two may be equal only when both are closed.

fields.name: lower
fields.description: The lowest stored value the conversion applies to, written as the scale's `LOWER-LIMIT`; omitted or `null` when the scale states none. An infinite limit is no bound: leave it out.

fields.name: upper
fields.description: The highest stored value the conversion applies to, written as the scale's `UPPER-LIMIT`; omitted or `null` when the scale states none. An infinite limit is no bound: leave it out.

kinds.description: One limit of a scale: a stored value and whether the limit itself belongs to the interval. A nested object rather than a list member, so it has no identity of its own and every field of it may change.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The limit's stored value. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float; it accepts neither NaN nor ±Infinity.

fields.name: interval
fields.description: Whether the limit belongs to the interval: `closed` (it does; the default, as an absent `INTERVAL-TYPE` is) or `open` (it does not). Written as the limit's `INTERVAL-TYPE`.

kinds.description: One named value of a `texttable`: a member of its `entries` collection, never a standalone element, so it has no file and no layer-level address. It has an enum literal's shape.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The entry's identity inside its table, written as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `SHORT-LABEL` and its `VT`, exactly as an enum literal's name; must not be blank, and immutable.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The integer the entry stands for, emitted as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `LOWER-LIMIT` and `UPPER-LIMIT`.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the entry. Written into the generated ARXML as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

layers.name: data_constraints
layers.description: Data constraints, one file each under `data_types/constraints/`: the physical limits a value is declared within, an element a type names by reference. One kind, `data_constr`, which an application type names as its `data_constr_ref`. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.
layers.label: Data Constraints

kinds.description: A data constraint, emitted as a `DATA-CONSTR` in `/DataTypes/Constraints` with one rule of `PHYS-CONSTRS`: the physical limits an application type is declared within. An application type names one by its `data_constr_ref`, in place of an inline `range`. It holds no internal limits.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The data constraint's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/constraints/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the data constraints, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name.

fields.name: min
fields.description: The lower physical limit; omitted or `null` when there is none. An integer is held as the integer it is; NaN and ±Infinity are refused.

fields.name: max
fields.description: The upper physical limit; omitted or `null` when there is none. An integer is held as the integer it is; NaN and ±Infinity are refused.

fields.name: level
fields.description: The rule's `CONSTR-LEVEL`, the category of the constraint (the lower the level, the more stringent the check); omitted or `null` when the rule states none.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the data constraint. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: package
fields.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Constraints`, its layer's package, this data constraint is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the data constraint and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Constraints/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Constraints` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

rules.summary: A `satisfies` member naming no declared requirement, or carrying a version that is not one: a member is `<id>@<version>`, the version a positive integer, or the bare `<id>`.
A requirement no `satisfies` member of any element names; a `derived_from` naming it is not an allocation.
A requirement that is a stub: named as a parent and never imported.
A `satisfies` or `derived_from` member naming a requirement by its bare `<id>`, with no `@<version>`.
A `satisfies` or `derived_from` member whose `@<version>` is not the named requirement's current `version`.
A `derived_from` member naming no declared requirement and no top-level element of a linkable layer, or carrying a version that is not one.
Requirements deriving from each other, through `derived_from`, in a cycle.
A decomposed requirement `X(Y)` whose `Y` is not the level before decomposition of a levelled requirement it derives from: that parent's own `(Y)` when it is decomposed, its level otherwise.
One `satisfies` or `derived_from` list naming one target twice: a requirement, at the same version or at two, or one element; each list names a target once.
A `satisfies` or `derived_from` member naming a requirement whose id holds `.`, which Sphinx-Needs reads as an id and a part: `generate needs` cannot publish the link.
An architecture requirement whose `title` or `description` is empty or whitespace only: it is published, and the requirements import refuses it.
Two connectors declaring the same name.
Two connectors declaring the same endpoint pair.
A connector endpoint naming no declared SWC.
A connector endpoint naming a port that component does not declare.
A connector's `from` endpoint is not a provide port.
A connector's `to` endpoint is not a require port.

A connector whose required port's interface is not satisfied by the provided port's: a kind that differs (an external interface stub's kind is the one its `external_dest` names), a data element or operation without a counterpart of the same name, or a counterpart whose resolved type or signature differs, a data element queued on one side only, or an `is_service` that differs. Not judged: an external interface stub beyond its kind, or whose `external_dest` is abstract; invalidValue, a value type's own unit and range, interface mappings.

A connector whose two ends are application components, followed through delegations across nested compositions, and whose interface carries a data element or an argument typed by a pointer, directly or through reference types: a pointer crosses a port only where one end is a service or an ECU-abstraction component. Not judged: an end that is an external component stub or that no delegation resolves to a component, and a pointer inside an implementation record or array.
A connector endpoint naming no declared composition.
A connector naming no declared composition.
A port of a component that is not an external stub naming no declared interface, or none at all (an external interface stub counts as declared).
A runnable access naming a port its component does not declare.
A runnable read or write naming no data element of the port's sender/receiver interface, or, through a port on an external interface stub, no name the stub lists in its `data_elements`.
A runnable call naming no operation of the port's client/server interface, or, through a port on an external interface stub, no name the stub lists in its `operations`.
A read or call through a provide port, or a write through a require port.
A read or write through a client/server port, or a call through a sender/receiver port.
An operation event naming a port its component does not declare.
An operation event through a require port.
An operation event through a port whose interface is sender/receiver.
An operation event naming no operation of the port's client/server interface, or, through a port on an external interface stub, no name the stub lists in its `operations`.
A `(port, operation)` pair named by more than one operation event of one component, on two runnables or twice on one.

A runnable started by operation events whose operations differ in argument count, in an argument's direction, or in the structure of an argument's resolved implementation type, position by position. Not judged: a position whose type does not resolve completely, or whose application type or enumeration the component's mapping sets do not map to exactly one implementation type; possible errors, the return value, errorHandling, serverArgumentImplPolicy and PortDefinedArgumentValues.

An external stub component declaring a port with an interface, measures or com-specs, runnables, variables, exclusive areas, a memory budget, data type mappings, a termination and restart handling, a package or a behaviour name.
An external stub with a blank or malformed `external_ref`/`external_dest`.
A component declaring `external_ref` or `external_dest` without `external: true`.
An external stub whose `external_ref` lies inside a package the generated ARXML declares the project's own elements in.
A component whose behaviour is emitted and that sets no `handle_termination_and_restart`, which AUTOSAR 4.2.2 and 4.3.0 require on every behaviour.

A port's `com_specs` entry naming no data element of the port's sender/receiver interface or, on a port typed by an external interface stub, no name the stub lists in its `data_elements`, or any entry on a port whose interface is client/server or undeclared.

A port's `com_specs` entry stating an attribute with no place on the port's side or the element's policy: a receiver-only attribute on a provide port, `queue_length` on an element that is not queued, a non-queued receiver attribute on a queued element, or an `init` on a queued element.

A port's `com_specs` entry for a data element an external interface stub lists that states an `init`, which the stub holds no type to shape, or, on a require port, a `queue_length`, since the com-spec of a stub's member is never queued.
A component's require port whose interface declares a queued data element and whose `com_specs` give that element no `queue_length`, which a queued receiver com-spec carries and nothing defaults.

An event's disabled mode whose `port` is not a require port of the component typed by an external interface stub with `external_dest` MODE-SWITCH-INTERFACE, or whose `mode_group_ref` does not lie directly under that stub's `external_ref`.
A runnable reading a queued data element `by: value`.

A component's variable whose `application_type` names no declared application type, or whose `implementation_type` names no declared implementation type (an external data type stub counts as declared).
A runnable's variable access naming no variable of its own component.

A component's variable typed by a pointer — named directly, at the end of a chain of reference types, or, for an application type, through the implementation type the component's mapping sets pair it with. A variable whose application type no set or more than one set pairs, or whose type is an external data type stub, is not judged.

A variable that a runnable of its component reads and that states no `init`: AUTOSAR leaves the value undefined when the read comes before every write, and the model states no order of execution, so no write can be shown to come first.
A runnable's `can_enter` or `runs_inside` entry naming no exclusive area of its own component.
A data-received event naming a port its component does not declare.
A data-received event through a provide port.
A data-received event through a port whose interface is client/server, or an external interface stub whose `external_dest` is not SENDER-RECEIVER-INTERFACE.
A data-received event naming no data element of the port's sender/receiver interface, or, through a port on an external interface stub, no name the stub lists in its `data_elements`.
A runnable reading a queued data element `by: implicit`: an implicit read takes one value before the runnable starts, and a queued element has no one value to take.
A runnable reading `by: implicit` a data element its port's `com_specs` entry states `enable_update: true` for.
One operation of one port called both synchronously and asynchronously by the runnables of one component.
The asynchronous calls of one operation of one port, by the runnables of one component, stating different timeouts — an absent `timeout` counting as a value of its own.

In a project generated at AUTOSAR 4.2.2, an asynchronous call that neither polls its result nor has a `call_returned` event naming its operation: 4.2.2 gives every asynchronous call point exactly one result point, where 4.3.0 allows none.
An asynchronous call with two result points — its own poll and a `call_returned` event naming its operation, or two such events: a call point is referenced by at most one result point.
A `call_returned` event naming an operation of a port that no runnable of its component calls asynchronously.
A `call_returned` event naming an operation that two or more runnables of its component call asynchronously, so no one call point is the one its result point references.
A runnable started by an `init` event that owns a result point — a call it polls or a `call_returned` event: a runnable an init event starts may call asynchronously but fetches no result.
A composition port typed by an interface that declares `is_service: true`.
An application type declaring a `conversion` and neither a `unit` nor a `unit_ref`: the conversion is written as a LINEAR compu method, which must refer to a unit.

A free text the model holds -- a `description`, a composition's `title`, a base type's `native_declaration` or `encoding`, an application type's `unit`, a unit's `display_name` -- containing a character XML 1.0 cannot carry (a NUL, a control character other than tab, line feed and carriage return, a lone surrogate, U+FFFE or U+FFFF), which no written document can hold as the model holds it.
A runnable stating a `symbol` that is not a C identifier: a letter or an underscore first, then letters, digits or underscores only.
Two runnables of one component written with one symbol — each runnable's `symbol`, or its name where it states none — compared exactly.

An external interface stub with a blank or malformed `external_ref` or one inside a package the generated ARXML declares the project's own elements in, or an `external_dest` that is not a port interface `DEST`.

An external data type stub with a blank or malformed `external_ref` or one inside a package the generated ARXML declares the project's own elements in, or an `external_dest` other than `IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE`.
The same data type name declared in more than one file of one layer.
A declared name colliding with the `_CompuMethod` generated for an enum that states `literals`, in the enum's package.

A sender/receiver data element whose `application_type` names no declared application type, or whose `implementation_type` names no declared implementation type (an external data type stub counts as declared).

A client/server argument whose `application_type` names no declared application type, or whose `implementation_type` names no declared implementation type (an external data type stub counts as declared).
An init value — a data element's own, a port's own in `com_specs`, or a component's variable's — whose shape the declared type cannot hold.

An init value — a data element's own, a port's own in `com_specs`, or a component's variable's — naming no literal of its declared enum type, or no entry of the table its declared value type or reference type references.
An init map — a data element's own, a port's own in `com_specs`, or a component's variable's — whose keys are not exactly its record type's fields or its implementation record's elements.
An init list — a data element's own, a port's own in `com_specs`, or a component's variable's — whose length is not its array or implementation array type's declared length.
An init value — a data element's own, a port's own in `com_specs`, or a component's variable's — outside the range its value type declares.
An init value — a data element's own, a port's own in `com_specs`, or a component's variable's — written as text where its declared type carries a number.
An init integer — a data element's own, a port's own in `com_specs`, or a component's variable's — too wide to be written out in full decimal digits.

An init value on a data element, or a port's own in `com_specs` for one, or on a component's variable, whose type is an external data type stub, named directly, through a chain of reference types, or as a member of an implementation record or array.
A value type whose `base` names no declared base type.
A reference type whose `base` names no declared type (an external data type stub counts as declared).
A record field naming no declared application type.
A record declaring one field name twice.
An array whose `element_type` names no declared application type.
An enum declaring one literal name twice.
An enum declaring one literal value twice.
A dependency cycle in the data-type graph.
The same task name declared in more than one file.
A task mapping naming no declared SWC.
A task mapping naming a runnable that component does not declare.
A runnable timing period that is not a positive multiple of its task's.
One runnable of one resolved component mapped by more than one task, whichever of `swc` and `instance` each entry names it by.

A component instance whose runnables are run by tasks of two or more partitions, judged per resolved instance: two occurrences of one type are two instances, and a type placed nowhere below the root composition is judged as one. Not judged without exactly one root composition or on a composition cycle.
A task mapping one runnable of one resolved component twice, through two entries written differently.
